Environment management · Lesson 0001

The process boundary

Predict whether Bun receives a variable before worrying about `.env`, Docker, or Cloudflare.

Target time: 6 minutes · Bash and Zsh

Your one mental model

An environment is a collection of text key–value pairs attached to a process. When your shell starts Bun, Bun is a child process. The shell chooses which values cross that boundary.

Parent
your shell
→
Child
Bun process
The rule: a normal shell variable stays in the shell. An exported variable is copied into subsequently started child processes. Changes do not travel backward from child to parent.

This behavior comes from the GNU Bash environment model and is shared by the Zsh use cases in this course.

Three ways to set a value

1. Shell-only

API_URL=https://local.example
bun -e 'console.log(process.env.API_URL)'  # undefined

The shell can expand $API_URL, but Bun does not inherit it.

2. Export for future children

export API_URL=https://local.example
bun -e 'console.log(process.env.API_URL)'  # https://local.example

The export attribute remains in this shell until you run unset API_URL, close the shell, or replace the value.

3. Give it to one command

API_URL=https://ci.example bun -e \
  'console.log(process.env.API_URL)'

This assignment is in Bun's environment only for that invocation. It does not modify the variable in your current shell. The Bash manual explicitly defines these command-scoped assignments.

Run the boundary experiment

Paste these commands into either Zsh or Bash:

LESSON_TOKEN=alpha
printf 'shell: %s\n' "$LESSON_TOKEN"
bun -e 'console.log("child:", process.env.LESSON_TOKEN)'

export LESSON_TOKEN
bun -e 'console.log("child:", process.env.LESSON_TOKEN)'

LESSON_TOKEN=beta bun -e \
  'console.log("one command:", process.env.LESSON_TOKEN)'
printf 'shell after: %s\n' "$LESSON_TOKEN"

unset LESSON_TOKEN

Expected sequence: shell prints alpha; first child prints undefined; exported child prints alpha; one command prints beta; shell still prints alpha.

Retrieval check

Answer before testing. Both answer buttons contain two words and eleven characters.

DEPLOY_ENV=staging

What happens when the shell later starts bun run deploy?

export DEPLOY_ENV=staging

What happens when the shell later starts bun run deploy?

DEPLOY_ENV=staging bun run deploy

What happens for this single Bun process?

A `.env` file is not an environment

It is only a text file. A tool must parse it, or a shell must execute compatible contents, before any process receives those values. Bun is such a tool: it automatically reads supported `.env` files. This distinction will explain most Bun-versus-npm surprises in the next lesson.
